largest._doc: The largest hook event: a payload of limits.payload_bytes, built as {"hook_event_name":<kind>,"prompt":"x..."} (the longest kind), sent as an event with seq and lost of 2^53 - 1. The event is event_bytes of JSON, within the 64 KiB a frame holds once the session is launched; a payload one byte larger is too-large.

mcp._doc: Tool stream vectors for docs/remote/helper-protocol.md section 15 (capability mcp, from 2.1.3-beta.10). Read by helper/tests/fixtures.rs and tests/unit/main/session-helper-protocol.test.ts. A request is read as a connection that acked core, local and mcp (the relay's ack) reads it, unless the vector says what was acked (acked). messages are the exact bytes the holder sends the app, and the app reads each as its fields say; invalid_messages are ones the app refuses. The limits on a message are for its message as compact JSON. offered and relay_caps are 2.1.3-beta.10's: what a holder offered then, and what a relay still acks a holder that does not offer away. A holder and a relay of 2.1.3-beta.12 are the away part's.

away._doc: Kept tool stream vectors for docs/remote/helper-protocol.md section 15 (capability away, from 2.1.3-beta.12). Read by helper/tests/fixtures.rs. offered is what a holder offered before screen reads (a holder of now: the status part's offered), relay_caps what a relay acks a holder that offers away. messages are the exact bytes the holder sends a relay that acked away: mcp.away when no connection takes its stream, mcp.back when one takes it again. answers are the exact lines the relay writes for its CLI in the app's place, without the line end: to a tools/call, and to any other call. The limits are the relay's: hold_secs is how long a held call waits in the build the installer ships, test_hold_secs in the build cargo test runs; held_bytes counts each held call as compact JSON.

screen._doc: Screen read vectors for docs/remote/helper-protocol.md section 15 (capability screen, from 2.1.3-beta.12). Read by helper/tests/fixtures.rs and tests/unit/main/session-helper-protocol.test.ts. offered is what a holder offered from 2.1.3-beta.14 until 2.1.3-beta.18 added status (a holder of now: the status part's offered). A request is read as a connection that acked core and screen reads it, unless the vector says what was acked (acked). Each of messages is the exact bytes a holder sends the app: its screen of cols by rows fed feed (the session's output from its first byte), then read (screen.rows, the answer to screen.read re) or its last count lines (screen.lines, the answer to screen.tail re); the app reads each as its json says. A message vector whose acked names screen and title is the answer to a connection that asked for the title (title in screen.rows, the title the feed last set, empty when it set none); any other is the answer to one that did not (no title). An invalid message is read the same way. invalid_messages are ones the app refuses. The limits: tail_lines is the most a screen.tail asks for, scrollback_lines what the screen keeps, param_ceiling the largest CSI parameter that reaches its parser, title_chars the most characters a title holds, answer_bytes the most JSON an answer is.

status._doc: Status line and hook kind vectors for docs/remote/helper-protocol.md section 15 (capability status, and hookKinds in a launch, from 2.1.3-beta.18). Read by helper/tests/fixtures.rs. offered is what a holder offers; status_caps what the status mode acks; env the variables the hook and status modes read a store and a session left out from. A request is read as a connection that acked core and status reads it, unless the vector says what was acked (acked), in a session whose launch declared the hook kinds in declared (null or none: it declared none, so the nine); a vector tagged os applies on that OS only (its paths). messages and taken are the exact bytes the holder sends; set is what the status mode sends for its standard input stdin. limits: payload_bytes the most a status payload is as compact JSON, stdin_bytes the most of standard input the status mode keeps, deadline_ms its deadline, round_ms the least time between two rounds of status, hook_kinds the most kinds a launch declares and hook_kind_chars the longest kind.
